# Vendored catalog

The site's firmware builder is Modwerk's own (`src/engine/elektron/builder.ts`: the worker, the linker, both OS file
families, module storage and the catalog). This folder holds what it serves and what is left to replace:

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `upstream-catalog.json` | the cores and mods Modwerk offers from upstream releases, cut to the library |
| `catalog/` | the pinned packages and `catalog.json`: `upstream-catalog.json` plus every module record `sdk/imports/elekloader-*.json`, generated by `npm ci` (`prepare`) and `npm run check`, never committed |
| `elekloader.lock.json` | the lock: `upstream-catalog.json` and the two kit files below by SHA-256 |
| `kit/kit.json` | the commit pin of the upstream checkout the Octatrack base's Python build tools still run (`npm run upstream:tools`) |
| `kit/src/codec/aplib.ts` | a re-export of Modwerk's packer that `sdk/machines/octatrack/elekloader/test_recipe.py` runs |

The two kit files go when the Octatrack base's build tools are Modwerk's own. `npm run elekloader:check` (part of
`npm run check`) checks the lock, that `catalog/catalog.json` is the upstream catalog plus every module record, every
pinned file, and refuses a package whose `jsr` or `jmp` to an absolute address has an odd target
(`src/engine/elektron/odd-jumps.ts`): a real unit stops there with an address error, while the emulators run on. The
site serves `catalog/` under `elekloader/`.

The catalog's `revision` identifies its set of cores and mods: for upstream-only updates the upstream revision; with
module records merged, a SHA-256 fingerprint of all the pins. Configuration backups record it; a backup naming an older
revision still imports, its modules looked up again in the library.

## Updating

Update by pull request, owner reviewed:

1. `npm run elekloader:update -- <catalog.json> [--library]` takes a full catalog: only Modwerk's machines, and with
   `--library` only the mods the library lists and what they require. Each file is downloaded from its source and
   checked against its pin; files already here with the pinned SHA-256 are kept.
2. A module's own pins are its record, `sdk/imports/elekloader-<id>-<date>.json`; after adding or changing one:
   `npm run elekloader:update -- --overlay sdk/imports/elekloader-<id>-<date>.json`.
3. The update stages and verifies the new catalog and lock first, then installs them, regenerates the notices and runs
   the vendor check; any failure restores every file. Do what it prints, run `npm run check`, and record the update in
   `docs/verification/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>.md`.

## Replaced kit files

Every kit file is now Modwerk's own code under `src/engine/elektron` and the kit's own copies are gone. One path
stays as a one-line re-export, `kit/src/codec/aplib.ts` of `src/engine/elektron/codec/pack.ts`, because the Octatrack
base's `test_recipe.py` runs it there and changing that file gives the base a new identity.
